draw_policy.default: frozen-instance-by-default: scripts/build_images.sh reads the Judge-only Infrathon asset judge/final_cases.json (INFRATHON_ASSETS_ROOT) unless FINAL_CASES_PATH names another instance; every host that builds from this tree evaluates the same cases
draw_policy.generator: scripts/generate_final_manifest.py converts a frozen, Judge-only suite plan; a new plan is a NEW suite identity
draw_policy.per_call_seeds: every warm-up, decoy, measured call and sequence round draws its group sizes and data from SHA-256(case seed, role, trial) truncated to 63 bits
draw_policy.redraw: a new frozen suite plan, converted by scripts/generate_final_manifest.py --plan PLAN --private-output OUT, is a NEW suite identity; no earlier score is comparable to it
draw_policy.privacy: model shapes, group-size parameters, hints and seeds are Judge-only; this repository and the Work image carry only opaque case IDs and families for the hidden suite

edge_suite.privacy: Judge-only Infrathon asset judge/edge_cases.json, staged mode 0600 into the root-only Judge build context with the scored cases, proven absent from every Work build context by scripts/validate_layout.py
edge_suite.semantics: untimed zero-weight hard gates over the whole support domain (any 1 <= M, N <= 8192, 1 <= G <= 128, group K 0 or a positive multiple of 128 with K_total <= 262144, any positive hint): each case is called twice on one fresh guarded input set; complete writes, the element-wise bound against the exact FP64 product (0.05 of the product scale), the per-group precision bound (2e-7) and the BF16-source metric (1e-3 on slices of at least 16384 outputs), guard bands and byte-exact inputs; the sanitize subset is also run once under compute-sanitizer memcheck with the caching allocator disabled

selection_semantics: the sanitizer subset of the edge cases runs first under compute-sanitizer memcheck, so an out-of-bounds kernel is stopped before any native call; then every edge case runs natively and must pass; then all 1082 scored cases run, each also a correctness and memory-safety gate; a single-call case is the median of 3 trials, a sequence case the median of 3 rounds (total flops / round time); within each of the four families cases are geometrically averaged per model and then across models, and the score is the geometric mean of the four family scores
timeout_semantics: suite gates and orchestration ceilings qualify the selected execution profile; they do not identify a GPU model

families.large: many tokens per expert (K per group >= 1024), K_total up to 262144; late-training (alpha 0.6-4) and early-training (alpha 0.1-0.3) routing imbalance
families.many_groups: 16 to 128 local experts at low expert parallelism, many groups small or empty
families.sequence: one backward pass of 58 layers, each issuing the second expert linear then the first, timed per round with no synchronization; group sizes redrawn on every call
families.small_batch: few tokens per expert (K per group < 1024); most groups one or two K blocks or empty

workload.group_sizes: Dirichlet(alpha) split of the case's fixed K_total into 128-row blocks with largest-remainder rounding, redrawn per call; calibrated synthetic load, not a routing capture
workload.hint: 1.2 * K_total / G * hint_scale; 96 cases carry a stale or badly wrong hint (x0.05 to x8)
workload.model_shapes: Judge and public cases use disjoint (M, N) shapes taken from public mixture-of-experts model configurations; Judge models are not named here
workload.trials: single-call cases: 1 warm-up, then 3 trials each preceded by an untimed decoy with redrawn group sizes; sequence cases: 1 untimed round, then 3 timed rounds
